title: Runtime Feedback Loops
service: FeedLog: a feedback runner that records each command's argv, redacted and truncated stdout and stderr, exit code, duration and agent note, writes the records to a size-rotated JSONL log, follows long-running commands live, and links retries into chains
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no network and no LLM: commands run against FakeShell (a scripted subprocess.run) and FakeProcess (a scripted asyncio subprocess), plus one real `python -c` run in Parts 1 and 4

parts.lesson_anchor: What goes in a feedback record; Refuse to advance without feedback (exit_code null and error); Redact at write, not at read; code/main.py run_with_feedback, _process_capture and loop_can_advance; quiz Q3, Q6, Q11, Q12
planted_bugs: the timeout branch puts TimeoutExpired.stdout (bytes) into the record unprocessed; the TypeError surfaces two calls away, in FeedbackRecord.to_json called from JsonlSink.append, and the output was neither redacted nor truncated
_capture truncates before it redacts: the 30-line cut drops the private key's BEGIN line, the multi-line pattern never matches and 27 key lines reach the record, although redact() itself is correct
a missing program is recorded with exit code 127, the shell's convention, so the correct loop_can_advance takes it for feedback; the assertion fails one call away from the cause
only FileNotFoundError is caught: a PermissionError escapes the runner and leaves no record
_decode decodes strictly, so binary output raises UnicodeDecodeError and loses the record
parts.timing_assert: none in this part; the timing assertion is in Part 3
parts.overfix_guard: exit code 1 must still let the loop advance (quiz Q3: rules out loop_can_advance as exit_code == 0); the timed-out output is kept, redacted and truncated (decoding only, dropping it, or not truncating are caught; decoding stdout only fails on stderr's bytes, and capturing stdout only leaves the password in stderr's dsn line); the private key must go while keyboard: us-intl, tokenizer=fast and the deploy_key lines stay (dropping lines with key or token, filtering base64-looking lines after truncating, and redacting line by line are caught); 127 taught to loop_can_advance is caught by exit_code is None; a script without a #! line raises a plain OSError (Exec format error), so catching FileNotFoundError and PermissionError only is caught; error is '<class>: <message>' and the timeout's error is built from timeout_s, not str(exc), which repeats the argv; errors='ignore', latin-1 and backslashreplace are caught; every command leaves exactly one record; cwd, timeout and parent reach the executor and the record; the exact argv list is kept

parts.lesson_anchor: Rotation policy, not a single file (cap per file, rotate to .1, .2, drop the oldest; the agent's loop reads only the current file, CI gets the full set); Exercise 3; Parent-command id lineage across rotated files; quiz Q8 and Q16
parts.storage: append-only JSONL: one record.to_json() line per record, UTF-8 with non-ASCII kept as is, in path and path.1 (newest) to path.<keep> (oldest)
parts.exactness: records read back equal, and every file's bytes are exactly the records' JSON lines; sizes are bytes on disk: records padded with a 4-byte emoji are 700 bytes but about 415 characters, two fit in an 1800-byte file, a 400-byte record fills one to exactly 1800, a 401-byte record after a 1400-byte file starts a new one (the newline counts), a 4000-byte record gets a file of its own and is never split
traps: rotating after the file has passed max_bytes, as the lesson's maybe_rotate does, or after writing the record that overflowed

parts.timing_assert: truncate_lines on a 60,000-line, 2.4 MB access log under 0.1 s. Measured on this machine in separate processes at load average 5 to 10: dropping the cut lines from the front of the string one at a time 1.10-1.28 s with Python 3.12 (11-13x the limit), 1.14-1.23 s with 3.10 and 1.14-1.30 s with 3.14; popping them from the front of a list 0.22-0.27 s (caught, 2.2-2.7x); the reference 2.0-5.2 ms with 3.12 (1/19 to 1/50 of the limit), 2.0-3.2 ms with 3.10 and 1.8-3.2 ms with 3.14. A character-by-character scan is linear but takes 40-60 ms with 3.12 and 3.14 and 90-160 ms with 3.10, so it can fail the limit (noted in INTERVIEWER.md)
parts.integration: the Part 1 runner with its default truncation (5 head and 30 tail lines) on output whose private key starts inside the head and ends inside the cut: the record keeps 5 + 30 lines of the redacted text and no key line, which needs Part 1's redact-before-truncate fix

parts.lesson_anchor: Every command goes through the runner; Truncation is deterministic (bounded head and tail); Refuse to advance without feedback (timeout gives exit_code null); A 50 MB log destroys the loop; code/main.py timeout branch
parts.wire_format: raw byte stream: an async generator of bytes, one yield per chunk with the lines it completed, each b'[stdout] ' or b'[stderr] ' plus the line's bytes as written plus b'\n', the unfinished last lines at the end, then the record alone as b'[record] ' plus one line of JSON; decided by the test's b''.join, split on b'\n' and json.loads

clarifying_questions: pipes closed but the process alive

parts.lesson_anchor: Parent-command id for retry chains (command_id, parent_command_id pointing at the previous attempt; the reviewer's failed-attempts list and the verification gate follow the chain); Exercise 4; Exercise 5 (highlight the latest non-zero exit); code/main.py retry_chain (a while loop over parent_command_id); rotation drops old parents (quiz Q8 and Q16: tell a chain's first attempt from a lost parent); quiz Q7
traps: a fork (one attempt retried twice) kept as one chain: a child-by-parent dict keeps only d3 or only d4, and a walked set shared by all chains stops the second fork at d2

last_failure: an attempt without an exit code counted as a failure, -9 not counted, the first failure instead of the latest, taken over the whole retry tree (both forks get d3), or set only when the last attempt failed

every record starting a chain, single attempts left out, attempts newest first, attempts as a list
duplicate ids or a retry of a later record accepted, only cycles rejected (a retry written before its parent without a cycle)

incidental, stated in the docstring (before and after mean position in records, never started_at): chains ordered by their first attempt or by started_at (the clock stepped back for a3), or a retry of a later record checked with started_at

deviations: Parts 1 and 3 swapped part of their content. The suggested Part 1 fixed _process_capture and deterministic_tail, and the suggested Part 3 implemented the same truncation and redaction again, so the same functions would have been tested twice. Here Part 3 implements truncate_lines from scratch (the lesson's core algorithm), with the suggested splitlines defect and the 50 MB quadratic tail as its traps and its timing assertion, and Part 1 debugs the runner around it. The suggested truncate-then-redact leak stays in Part 1 as a defect in the runner's _capture; the Part 1 test passes a tail-only truncation of its own, so Part 1 does not depend on Part 3, and Part 3 ends with the suggested scenario (BEGIN line in the head, END line in the cut) on the real truncation. The keyboard layout and tokenizer=fast guard is kept in Part 1.

The suggested Part 1 defect of rotated files sorted by name (.10 and .11 before .2) moved to Part 2, which writes and reads the rotated files, as a trap with keep=12. Part 1 instead gets three defects from the lesson's own pitfalls: TimeoutExpired output stored as bytes (the error two calls away), 127 for a missing program (quiz Q6), only FileNotFoundError caught (quiz Q12), plus strict decoding. Monotonic durations and argv normalisation were left out because lessons 35 and 38 own them. Part 1 has no timing assertion; Part 3 has it.

Part 2: append-only JSONL as assigned. Per-pattern redaction counts were left out (the record keeps per-stream counts as in code/main.py). The U+2028 and str.splitlines() trap for JSONL is not used here because lesson 08 of this chapter already uses it and Part 3 uses the splitlines trap for truncation; it is a follow-up question instead.

Part 4: raw byte stream as assigned. The fake process has two pipes that each hold one write, so reading the pipes one after the other deadlocks as it would with a real full pipe, and the follower also runs against a real asyncio subprocess. Nothing is redacted in the live view (stated in the docstring), so cross-chunk redaction stays with chapter 13 lesson 26; besides the suggested traps, the deadline covers waiting for the exit, and an unfinished line still goes out at the deadline.

Part 5: as suggested (roots, the last attempt's exit code, the latest non-zero exit, orphaned instead of an error, forks, order by the chain's last attempt), with -9 counted as a failure and an exit code of None not, and duplicate ids and retries of later records rejected. The test centres on what the lesson's parent_command_id chains bring: forks, chains orphaned by rotation, the latest real failure and a 1500-attempt polling chain that rules out recursion. Order is position in records, never started_at, and the docstring says so; a3, whose clock stepped back, stays as a side check, because lessons 09 and 24 of this chapter already centre on write order against a skewed clock.
